s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly growing caruncular lesion with ulceration
salient_findings: Amelanotic, pedunculated mass with ulcerated surface
Large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
key_facts: Male patient in his late 60s
4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
Medical and ocular histories were unremarkable
Ocular examination findings were normal except for the caruncular lesion
No evidence of primary acquired melanosis (PAM)
Specimen measured 8 × 6 × 5 mm with a 4-mm ulceration
Necrotic tissue on the surface of the specimen
Solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface
Positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
Significant number of cycling cells shown by Ki-67 proliferation marker
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor

raw.syndrome_frame: Rapidly growing caruncular lesion with ulceration
salient_findings: Amelanotic, pedunculated mass with ulcerated surface
Large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
key_facts: Male patient in his late 60s
4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
Medical and ocular histories were unremarkable
Ocular examination findings were normal except for the caruncular lesion
No evidence of primary acquired melanosis (PAM)
Specimen measured 8 × 6 × 5 mm with a 4-mm ulceration
Necrotic tissue on the surface of the specimen
Solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface
Positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
Significant number of cycling cells shown by Ki-67 proliferation marker
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor

raw.rationale: The presence of a rapidly growing, ulcerated caruncular lesion with positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A, and a high proliferative index as shown by Ki-67, strongly supports the diagnosis of amelanotic melanoma.

rejected.label: sarcoma
rejected.why: While sarcomas can present as rapidly growing lesions, the specific immunohistochemical markers and the context of the caruncular location more strongly support melanoma.

rejected.label: angiosarcoma
rejected.why: There is no mention of vascular differentiation or specific markers for angiosarcoma, making this less likely than melanoma.

rejected.label: leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: The lack of smooth muscle differentiation markers and the presence of melanocytic markers make leiomyosarcoma an unlikely diagnosis.

rejected.label: malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
rejected.why: There is no indication of nerve sheath origin or specific markers for this tumor type, making it less likely than melanoma given the provided information.
